verdict.reasoning: Patient states the wheeze started about two days ago: "it started, like, about two days ago" and it is ongoing.

Patient links onset to house cleaning and dust: "it started, like, about two days ago... I was, like, cleaning the house and, like, all this dust came out of the carpet... don't know if it was triggered by".
Patient notes nocturnal worsening: "Yeah, so it gets a bit worse at night, I find."
Patient reports shortness of breath and difficulty finishing sentences: "I'm feeling, like, a little bit short of breath" and "sometimes I'm unable to complete my sentences".
Doctor asks about pain with deep breath: "do you notice any pain?" Patient replies "No, no. No pain." Chest pain specifically is not mentioned, so denying chest pain is not explicit.
Doctor asks about dizziness: "have you noticed yourself feeling dizzy or the room spinning"; patient replies: "No, no dizziness? None of that."
Patient reports intake: "Yeah, yeah, I think I'm having, like, you know, four or five glasses a day."
Patient says: "I used to have, like, a bit of asthma as a child" indicating childhood asthma history.
Patient reports: "also in the summer, I sometimes get hay fever."

Patient says she still has an inhaler but timing is different: "I have, like, an asthma inhaler" and later "I think I might have one from like a couple of months ago." The fact adds it is a short-acting beta-agonist and that it has not been used for a couple of months, which are not stated. "From like a couple of months ago" refers to when she got it, not use.
When asked about allergies: "apart from this, do you know if you're allergic to anything?" Patient replies: "Not that I know of." This corresponds to no known allergies.
Doctor frames assessment as asthma vs allergy: "given you've got a history of asthma and hay fever, this could be one of two things, but we want to rule out asthma or an allergy first."
Doctor advises in-person clinic visit: "what you need is visit one of our clinics so we can do some more tests" and confirms proximity to a doctor’s surgery.
Doctor only specifies oxygen saturation: "use a small device on your finger to check the amount of oxygen in your blood." A full respiratory examination is not mentioned.

Doctor advises antihistamine before/while going: "if you've got something like an antihistamine... at home, I would take one" and suggests obtaining one on the way: "you might be able to get one on your way to the doctor's surgery."
Doctor says steroids may be needed depending on test results: "you may need to take some steroids now. But... we won't be able to know until we've done those tests first."
Doctor states: "I'm going to write a letter for your GP" and later: "You should get the letter over the app and then... take yourself to the gp."
